summary: Portugal follows Schengen area rules. EU nationals can travel there with a valid passport or a national identity card. Nationals of the countries listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries listed in Annex I need a visa; the Visa Code sets the visa fee at EUR 90. faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Portugal?
faq.answer: No. The EU's ETIAS website lists the United States among the visa-exempt countries whose nationals will need an ETIAS travel authorisation, and Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 exempts nationals of the countries in its Annex II from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. ETIAS is not yet in operation; the official ETIAS website lists a EUR 20 application fee.

faq.question: How much does a Portugal Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Visa Code sets the visa fee at EUR 90, and at EUR 45 for children from six to under 12; the fee is waived for children under six. A visa under the Visa Code is for an intended stay on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period, and a uniform visa is valid for the entire territory of the Member States.

faq.question: What income do I need for Portugal's residency visa for people living from passive income?
faq.answer: For passive income, Portugal's visa portal asks for a document certifying revenue from movable and immovable property, intellectual or financial assets, and it bases means of subsistence on the minimum monthly salary: 920€ in 2026 for the first adult. The national visa fee is €110, and the Foreigners Act says the residence visa allows its holder to enter Portugal in order to apply for a residence permit.

faq.question: Does Portugal have a digital nomad visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Portugal's visa portal lists a residency visa for the exercise of a professional activity done remotely (digital nomads). It asks for proof of average monthly income for the last three months with a minimum value equivalent to four monthly minimum guaranteed remunerations. The national visa fee is €110.
